notation.meaning: Vacancy rate, vacancies per member of the labor force
Elasticity of hires with respect to unemployment
Unemployed and employed workers in period $t$

blocks.md: When firms advertise lots of job openings, few people tend to be unemployed; when openings are scarce, many are. Plotting the vacancy rate against the unemployment rate traces a downward-sloping curve, named after the economist William Beveridge. In a search model the reason is simple: more openings per jobseeker means each jobseeker finds work faster, so fewer people are waiting at any moment. The curve shifts outward when matching gets worse, for example if workers' skills no longer fit the openings, or when jobs end more often: then both more openings and more unemployment coexist.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: Its downward slope is a persistent feature of real data that search models reproduce, and outward shifts signal a market that matches poorly.
Combining steady-state unemployment with the matching function's job-finding rate:
A higher tightness $\theta = V/U$ means a lower $\bar{u}$; since the vacancy rate is $v = \theta\bar{u}$, higher vacancies go with lower unemployment along the curve.

| Change | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Tightness $\theta$ ↑ (firms post more vacancies) | Move along the curve: $\bar{u}$ ↓, $v$ ↑ |
| Separation rate $\lambda$ ↑ | Curve shifts out (right, with $\theta$ on the vertical axis and $\bar{u}$ on the horizontal): higher $\bar{u}$ at every $\theta$ |
| Matching efficiency $A$ ↓ | Curve shifts out (right); a rise in $A$ shifts it in (left) |

- **Treating a move along the curve as a shift.** A change in $\theta$ alone moves the economy along a given curve; only $\lambda$ or $A$ (or another matching parameter) shifts it.
- **Reading the curve as causal from unemployment to vacancies.** Both are outcomes; tightness is set elsewhere in the model (vacancy creation and wages).
- Labor macroeconomics: diagnosing matching efficiency (outward shifts after recessions), the [Diamond-Mortensen-Pissarides Model](note:diamond-mortensen-pissarides-model).
